chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Attar, from Asim ibn Jamil, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three types of people Allah will not speak to on the Day of Judgment, nor will He look at them, nor purify them, and they will have a painful punishment: an aged fornicator, a despotic ruler, and a proud poor person.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the three types of people Allah will not speak to on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal* highlights the spiritual decay of three distinct social classes: the elderly who fail to leverage their experience for wisdom, the powerful who abuse their authority, and the poor whose lack of wealth does not excuse their arrogance. In Shia tradition, this triad illustrates how pride (*kibr*) manifests differently across age, status, and economic standing, serving as a warning against the corruption of character regardless of one's position in society.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 12.  Imam  Muhammad  Baqir  (a.s.)  narrates  that  the  Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) said, “Allah will not talk to three types of people on the Day of Judgment and neither will He send mercy upon them. They will not be consoled and shall get severe punishment. Those three are – an aged fornicator, a despotic ruler and person who is proud.”
